lines.name: Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040), no headers

spec.regulator: 3V3(OUT): keep the external load under 300 mA (Pico datasheet)
spec.source: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, mechanical drawing

alternates: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (SC1631, RP2350, same size and pinout; use the CircuitPython build for the Pico 2)
lines.notes: Wires are soldered straight to its castellated pads, so the plain board without headers is the one to buy.

lines.name: Adafruit SCD-40 True CO2, Temperature and Humidity Sensor, STEMMA QT

spec.holes: 4 x 3.0 mm, 2.54 mm in from each edge (20.32 x 17.78 mm apart)
spec.header: 5 x 0.1 in holes on the bottom edge: VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA
spec.source: adafruit.com/product/5187, Adafruit-SCD-4x-PCB board file, Sensirion SCD4x datasheet D1

alternates: Adafruit 5190 (SCD-41: 400-5000 ppm, same board, about 5 USD more)

lines.name: Adafruit Monochrome 0.96 in 128x64 OLED Graphic Display, STEMMA QT

spec.panel: UG-2864HSWEG01, 26.70 x 19.26 x 1.45 mm, active area 21.744 x 10.864 mm
spec.boardMm: 29.21 x 31.75 (board file; the product page says 29.2 x 26.7)
spec.source: adafruit.com/product/326, Adafruit-128x64-Monochrome-OLED-PCB 'Adafruit 0.96in 128x64 OLED STEMMA QT.brd', UG-2864HSWEG01 datasheet

lines.notes: A generic 0.96 in SSD1306 I2C module costs less but has another board size and hole pattern, so the front shell would need its params changed (sprue edit).

lines.name: Bi-colour LED, 5 mm, red/green, white diffused, common cathode

spec.colours: hyper red 630 nm + green 570 nm, AlGaInP
spec.source: Kingbright WP59SURKCGKW (was L-59SURKCGKW) listings and datasheet

lines.name: Resistor, 390 ohm, 1/4 W, through-hole

spec.use: one in series with each LED anode: about 3.5 mA red and 3.1 mA green at 3.3 V

lines.notes: Any 390 ohm 1/4 W through-hole resistor works; most shops sell them in tens.

lines.name: STEMMA QT / Qwiic JST SH 4-pin cable, 100 mm

spec.connector: JST SH 4-pin, 1 mm pitch, both ends

lines.name: Silicone hook-up wire, 26 AWG stranded, a few colours

spec.needMm: about 450 (4 x 50 mm to the sensor, 3 x 80 mm to the LED, spare)

lines.notes: Any 24 to 28 AWG stranded wire you already have does the job.

lines.name: USB cable, USB-A to micro-B, 1 m

spec.data: must carry data, not charge only (code.py is copied over it)

lines.notes: Skip it if you have a micro-B data cable whose moulding is at most 11 x 8 mm.

lines.name: Front shell (front wall, sides, corner columns)

spec.features: OLED window 24.4 x 13.5 mm, 5.2 mm LED hole, micro-USB opening 12.5 x 9.5 mm in the right side, OLED ledge and two M2 bosses, four corner columns with 4.0 mm insert holes

lines.name: Back lid (carries the Pico and the sensor)

spec.features: five vent slots over the sensor, five intake slots low down, 4 mm Pico standoffs, 7.5 mm sensor standoffs, four 3.4 mm screw holes

lines.name: Brass heat-set insert, M3 x 4 mm
M3 x 6 mm button head screw, ISO 7380
M2 x 6 mm pan head Phillips screw, ISO 7045

spec.head: pan, Phillips, ISO 7045
spec.use: 2 for the Pico, 2 for the sensor

lines.name: M2 x 4 mm pan head Phillips screw, ISO 7045

spec.source: Adafruit 550 page: about 8 mm across and 4 mm tall
